rules.description: The AppData folder holds the settings and data of all your programs; the folder itself is never offered for deletion.
rules.source: Well-known Windows profile layout

rules.description: The Roaming folder holds settings that follow your account; the folder itself is never offered for deletion.
rules.source: Well-known Windows profile layout

rules.description: The Local folder holds program data for this computer; the folder itself is never offered for deletion.
rules.source: Well-known Windows profile layout

rules.description: The LocalLow folder holds data of low-integrity programs; the folder itself is never offered for deletion.
rules.source: Well-known Windows profile layout

rules.description: The Microsoft folder in Roaming holds data of Windows and Microsoft programs; the folder itself is never offered for deletion.
rules.source: Well-known Windows profile layout

rules.description: The Microsoft folder in Local holds data of Windows and Microsoft programs; the folder itself is never offered for deletion.
rules.source: Well-known Windows profile layout

rules.description: The Packages folder holds the data of your Microsoft Store apps; the folder itself is never offered for deletion.
rules.source: Well-known Windows profile layout

rules.description: The Programs folder holds programs installed for your account only; the folder itself is never offered for deletion.
rules.source: Well-known Windows profile layout

rules.description: Windows keys that protect your saved passwords and encrypted data. Deleting them makes that data unreadable.
rules.source: Windows Data Protection API (DPAPI) master key location

rules.description: Credentials stored by Windows for your account.
rules.source: Windows Credential Manager storage location

rules.description: Credentials stored by Windows for your account on this computer.
rules.source: Windows Credential Manager storage location

rules.description: Your certificates and trust settings.
rules.source: Windows certificate store location in the user profile

rules.description: Your cryptographic keys.
rules.source: Windows cryptography key storage location in the user profile

rules.description: The Windows password vault.
rules.source: Windows Credential Manager storage location

rules.description: Your Start menu shortcuts and folders.
rules.source: Well-known Windows profile layout

rules.description: App execution aliases and links of Microsoft Store apps.
rules.source: Well-known Windows profile layout

rules.description: SSH private keys and known hosts. Losing a key can lock you out of servers and code hosting accounts, so it is kept.
rules.source: OpenSSH for Windows documentation (Microsoft Learn): user keys in %USERPROFILE%\.ssh

rules.description: GnuPG keys and trust data (gnupg in Roaming is the Gpg4win location). Losing a private key means encrypted data can no longer be read.
rules.source: GnuPG documentation: home directory (.gnupg); Gpg4win uses %APPDATA%\gnupg

rules.description: AWS CLI credentials and settings. They give access to cloud accounts, so they are kept.
rules.source: AWS CLI documentation: configuration and credential file settings (~/.aws)

rules.description: Azure CLI sign-in tokens and settings. They give access to cloud accounts, so they are kept.
rules.source: Azure CLI documentation (Microsoft Learn): the Azure CLI configuration folder ~/.azure

rules.description: Kubernetes configuration with cluster addresses and credentials.
rules.source: Kubernetes documentation: organizing cluster access using kubeconfig files (~/.kube/config)

rules.description: Docker CLI settings, including registry sign-ins.
rules.source: Docker documentation: Docker CLI configuration files (~/.docker/config.json)

rules.description: Android debug signing key and adb keys. The folder can also hold emulator images and be large; remove it by hand if you are sure you no longer need it.
rules.source: Android developer documentation: sign your app (debug keystore in ~/.android) and adb keys

rules.description: Crypto wallets. Losing a wallet file can mean losing the money in it.
rules.source: Well-known location of the wallet programs' data folders (Bitcoin Core, Electrum, Exodus, Ethereum clients)

rules.description: Installer cache. Uninstalling and repairing installed programs needs these files.
rules.source: Well-known location of the Windows Installer / Burn bootstrapper package cache

rules.description: UAC file virtualization. Data of older programs that cannot write to protected folders lives here.
rules.source: Microsoft Learn: User Account Control file and registry virtualization

rules.description: .NET isolated storage. Settings of many small programs live here.
rules.source: Microsoft Learn: Isolated storage (.NET)

rules.description: Folders of Windows components in your profile. Windows creates and uses them itself.
rules.source: Well-known location of Windows components in %LOCALAPPDATA% (not documented individually)

rules.description: DirectX shader cache. The folder itself is never offered for deletion.
rules.source: Well-known location of the DirectX shader cache
